evidence.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Education
evidence.scope: England education-sector position, principally aimed at schools and colleges; the Department notes that some considerations are relevant to other stages.
evidence.summary: The guidance describes possible teacher-facing uses and advises professional judgement over AI outputs, data protection and attention to intellectual property and assessment integrity.
limitations: This is an England example, focused on schools and colleges; its legal statements do not establish UAE requirements or university assessment rules.
The guidance is updated over time; the linked page was last updated on 12 August 2025.
evidence.source_locator: Opportunities and challenges; Using AI responsibly: Data privacy; Intellectual property; Formal assessments
evidence.verification: Official source reviewed on 2026-11-04; confirm updates before consequential use.

evidence.title: Assessment reform for the age of artificial intelligence
evidence.authority: Tertiary Education Quality and Standards Agency (TEQSA)
evidence.scope: Expert-developed, non-prescriptive guidance for Australian higher education on assessment in a generative-AI context.
evidence.summary: TEQSA’s expert paper offers guiding principles and propositions for assessment design that both assure learning and prepare students to engage ethically with generative AI.
limitations: The paper describes directions for the sector, not a mandatory formula or a UAE policy.
Related TEQSA resources appeared in 2025 and 2026; this entry is the 2023 paper.
evidence.source_locator: Guiding principles pp. 2–3; propositions pp. 3–6; conclusion p. 6
evidence.verification: TEQSA publication page and PDF pp. 2–6 reviewed 2026-11-05; https://www.teqsa.gov.au/sites/default/files/2023-09/assessment-reform-age-artificial-intelligence-discussion-paper.pdf.

evidence.title: Outcomes-Based Evaluation Framework University Guide
evidence.authority: Commission for Academic Accreditation, Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research
evidence.scope: Higher education institutional evaluation and accreditation guidance, including learning outcomes; not a classroom AI or assessment tool standard.
evidence.summary: CAA describes an outcomes-based quality assurance framework for universities and data used for licensure and accreditation renewal.
limitations: Overview does not establish requirements for AI-generated assessments, student records or support.
The former 2019 standards page was inaccessible; the relationship and detailed current provisions were not verified.

evidence.verification: CAA public overview and licensure page checked 2026-11-05. This record does not assert that a particular institution is subject to the framework.

evidence.title: Federal Decree by Law No. (45) of 2021 Concerning the Protection of Personal Data
evidence.authority: United Arab Emirates Government, UAE Legislation
evidence.scope: Federal personal-data framework, subject to its territorial scope, exclusions and applicable regulations; potentially relevant when education tools process identifiable student or staff data.
evidence.summary: The federal law regulates personal-data processing and sets processing controls, individual rights and conditions for transfers, subject to its scope and exceptions.
limitations: Article 2 excludes government data and government entities processing personal data, certain regulated health and banking data, and free-zone establishments with their own data-protection legislation. Do not assume this federal regime applies to every university.
Article references are starting points, not a complete account of duties, exceptions, implementing rules or later changes; verify the authoritative Arabic text and current instruments.
Current statutory full text, cross-border transfer conditions and applicability to this prototype have not been verified.
evidence.source_locator: Articles 2–5 (scope and processing controls); Articles 13–19 (data-subject rights); Articles 22–23 (cross-border transfer)
evidence.verification: Official indexed provisions corroborated on 2026-11-04; direct page returned HTTP 403 in this review. Full current text and amendments require further verification.

evidence.title: Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act regulations
evidence.scope: Educational agencies or institutions receiving funds under a program administered by the U.S. Secretary of Education; covers defined education records, including in postsecondary institutions.
evidence.summary: FERPA rules provide eligible students access and amendment rights and regulate disclosures of personally identifiable information from education records, including exceptions to prior consent.
limitations: FERPA is US law and is not a general UAE rule. Not every recording or transcript necessarily meets the education-record definition.
At a postsecondary institution FERPA rights generally transfer to the eligible student; consent has exceptions, including a conditioned school-official exception.
evidence.verification: Department of Education regulatory text reviewed 2026-11-05.

evidence.title: AI Ethics Self-Assessment Tool
evidence.scope: Voluntary beta self-assessment for organisations developing or operating AI systems, based on the UAE AI Ethics Principles and Guidelines; not specific to education.
evidence.summary: The tool encourages assessment of ethical issues throughout an AI system's lifecycle, including data use, accountability, third-party methods and bias.
limitations: The source calls its recommendations non-compulsory and the tool beta; a self-assessment score is not a government audit, approval or certification.
General AI ethics guidance does not replace applicable law or university-specific policies.

The underlying Principles and Guidelines are non-binding and section 1.2 targets significant or critical decisions; ordinary rehearsal uses them as voluntary design guidance, not a compliance obligation.
evidence.source_locator: What is the self-assessment tool for?; What does it contain?
evidence.verification: Official source reviewed on 2026-11-04; confirm updates before consequential use.

evidence.title: Federal Law No. (29) of 2006 Concerning the Rights of Persons with Special Needs
evidence.authority: United Arab Emirates Government, UAE Legislation
evidence.scope: Federal disability-rights law; its education provisions address education across institutions and include the Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research.
evidence.summary: The education provisions address equal educational opportunities for persons with disabilities and the role of education authorities in meeting their needs.
limitations: The English source uses historical terminology; use respectful current terminology in the product.
Review amendments, implementing measures and the authoritative current text before making legal determinations; this entry does not specify a technical accessibility standard.
evidence.verification: Official indexed provisions corroborated on 2026-11-04; direct page returned HTTP 403 in this review. Full current text and amendments require further verification.

evidence.title: National Policy for Digital Accessibility
evidence.authority: Telecommunications and Digital Government Regulatory Authority (TDRA)
evidence.scope: Article 3 covers federal entities and specified regulated or government-connected parties; local, semi-government and private entities are also asked to consider it with best efforts. Coverage of a particular private university is not established.
evidence.summary: A scoped digital-services policy. Annex 1 specifies WCAG 2.1 Level AA for public-service sites within that policy context.
limitations: Do not assert blanket applicability to all private universities or all classroom activities.
A citation or automated review does not establish WCAG conformance or legal compliance.
evidence.source_locator: PDF page 7, Article 3; PDF page 13, Annex 1 section 1. Issue date: March 2024.
evidence.verification: Official PDF scope and annex pages extracted and visually checked on 2026-11-04; this is not PDPL or institutional applicability verification.

evidence.title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2: captions
evidence.scope: Web accessibility technical standard, not education-specific; applies to synchronized media as specified in the success criteria.
evidence.summary: WCAG 2.2 calls for captions for prerecorded synchronized media audio, subject to a labelled text-alternative exception, and for live synchronized media audio.
limitations: A technical standard does not itself establish UAE legal duties; the US Title II rule separately incorporates WCAG 2.1 AA.
The prerecorded criterion excludes media that is a clearly labelled media alternative for text. Captions alone do not establish overall accessibility.
evidence.source_locator: Success Criteria 1.2.2 Captions (Prerecorded), Level A; 1.2.4 Captions (Live), Level AA
